ja_text:
金のためなら
赤子も喜んで殺すらしい
en_text:
They say she'd happily slaughter
her own child for coin!
ar_text_before: يقال إنها مستعدة لقتل طفل رضيع من أجل المال.
ar_text_gemini: يقال إنها تقتل طفلاً رضيعًا بكل سرور من أجل المال.
final_ar_text: يقال إنها تقتل طفلاً رضيعًا بكل سرور من أجل المال.
notes: '喜んで殺す' = kill gladly/happily. Before ('مستعدة لقتل' = willing/ready to kill) shifts meaning to willingness rather than the actual enjoyment in killing. After ('تقتل...بكل سرور') correctly conveys the gladness/glee, matching EN 'happily slaughter'.

STYLE_GUIDE.md: 'Ellipsis … (single char), preserve count for pacing.' Source ja_text has 4 consecutive U+2026 characters (verified: len=4). Before used 12 ASCII dots (=4 units of '...', arguably matching count if read as 3-dot groups, but wrong character per style guide). Gemini's 'after' uses only 2 unicode ellipsis chars, undercounting the source's 4-char run despite the stated reason claiming '4 dots' — internally inconsistent with its own output. Correct fix should use exactly 4 unicode ellipsis characters to preserve count as the style guide requires.

ja_text: お花はいかがですか？
en_text: Would you like a flower?
ar_text_before: هل ترغب في الحصول على زهور؟
ar_text_gemini: هل ترغب في الحصول على زهرة؟
final_ar_text: هل ترغب في الحصول على زهرة؟
notes: EN uses singular 'a flower', and the follow-up line (id=23, '花らしい' = 'a single flower') confirms she is selling one flower at a time. Singular 'زهرة' is the accurate, contextually consistent choice.

Identical case to id=18 — ja_text is 4 unicode ellipsis chars, Gemini's 2-char output undercounts against STYLE_GUIDE.md's 'preserve count' rule. Correct final text needs 4 unicode ellipsis characters.

ja_text:
ずいぶんお高い
花らしい
en_text: Pretty steep for a single flower.
ar_text_before:
إنها باهظة الثمن للغاية
يا لها من زهرة
ar_text_gemini: إنها باهظة الثمن للغاية لزهرة واحدة.
final_ar_text: إنها باهظة الثمن للغاية لزهرة واحدة.
notes: Before was a garbled two-line fragment ('how expensive... what a flower!') that loses the comparative meaning 'expensive FOR a single flower'. After is a single clear sentence matching both ja_text and en_text precisely.

en_text: Um...
notes: Same ellipsis-count issue as id=18/20. ja_text is 4 unicode ellipsis characters; Gemini's 'after' (2 chars) still undercounts per STYLE_GUIDE.md. Correct final text: 4 unicode ellipsis characters.

ja_text: 誰に頼まれて売っている？
en_text: Who put you up to this?
ar_text_before: لمن تبيعينها بناءً على طلب من أحد؟
notes: Before was an awkward/garbled construction mixing 'to whom' with 'based on someone's request' that doesn't parse cleanly in Arabic. After is a clean, natural, accurate rendering of '誰に頼まれて' (who asked you to) while correctly preserving the feminine addressee marker (منكِ).

ja_text: それは……
en_text: I...I can't...
ar_text_before: هذا...
notes: This is an interpretive leap beyond the literal ja ('that is...'), but it matches the official en_text's adaptation ('I...I can't...') and fits the scene (flower girl being pressured/interrogated, trailing off in inability to answer). 'هذا...' (literal 'this...') doesn't convey the implied hesitation/inability that both the EN localization and dialogue context call for.

ja_text:
だけど……
これを売らないと……
en_text:
But they said that if I don't
sell this...
ar_text_before:
ولこن...
إذا لم أبع هذا...
notes: Each ja ellipsis run is exactly 2 unicode '…' characters. Before used 3 ASCII dots per run (non-compliant with STYLE_GUIDE.md's 'single char' unicode ellipsis rule). After correctly uses 2 unicode ellipsis characters per run, matching the source count exactly.

ja_text: 弟たちが……
en_text: My brothers... They'll...
ar_text_before: إخوتي...
notes: ja ellipsis run is 2 unicode '…' characters. After correctly switches from 3 ASCII dots to 2 unicode ellipsis characters, matching source count and the style guide's unicode-ellipsis rule.

ja_text:
やれやれだ……
結局こうなるもんな
en_text: How did I know this was coming?
ar_text_before:
يا للهول...
في النهاية ينتهي الأمر هكذا
ar_text_gemini:
يا إلهي...
في النهاية ينتهي الأمر هكذا
final_ar_text:
يا إلهي...
في النهاية ينتهي الأمر هكذا
notes: 'やれやれ' is a tired/resigned sigh ('sheesh', 'well, well') — NOT an expression of horror. Before ('يا للهول' = 'how horrifying!') wrongly injects a fear/shock register the source doesn't have. After ('يا إلهي' = 'oh good grief/my god') correctly reads as resigned exasperation, matching GAME_CONTEXT.md's confirmed 'grounded, not overwrought' tone.

Same source ja_text (4 unicode ellipsis chars, verified len=4) as id=18/20/25, yet here Gemini's 'after' reverted to 6 ASCII dots and its stated reason claims '6 dots' — inconsistent both with the actual source count (4, not 6) and with unicode-ellipsis-only compliance (STYLE_GUIDE.md forbids ASCII dot sequences). Correct final text: 4 unicode ellipsis characters, consistent with the identical id=18/20/25 lines.

ja_text: ……来るぞ
en_text: ...Here they come!
ar_text_before: ...إنه قادم.
notes: EN explicitly uses plural 'they come', and this is a combat-warning line about an incoming enemy group (typical ambush/encounter context). Plural 'إنهم قادمون' matches both the EN gloss and the typical multi-enemy encounter framing; singular 'إنه قادم' understates the threat.

ja_text:
ひいぃ……
おい、退くぞ！
en_text:
No-good scoundrels!
You'll pay for this!
ar_text_before:
هيه...
هيا، تراجعوا!
notes: 'ひいぃ' is a whimper/gasp of fear. 'هيه' is not a standard Arabic interjection and reads oddly; 'آهٍ' is an established Arabic exclamation of pain/distress and renders the fear-whimper more naturally, without changing the accompanying 'let's retreat' line.

Same issue as id=39 — identical ja_text (4 unicode ellipsis chars) to id=18/20/25, but Gemini output 6 ASCII dots with the same mismatched '6 dots' reasoning. Correct final text: 4 unicode ellipsis characters.

ja_text:
あんな子供にまで
“粉”を売らせるのか
en_text:
Using children to peddle their
poison, are they now?
ar_text_before: هل يبيعون "المسحوق" حتى للأطفال؟
notes: '売らせる' is the causative form of 売る ('sell') = 'make [someone] sell'. Before mistranslated this as selling TO children (reversing subject/object: children as buyers). After correctly uses a causative construction ('يجعلون الأطفال يبيعون' = 'make the children sell'), matching both ja_text's causative grammar and en_text's 'using children to peddle'. This is a genuine mistranslation fix, not a stylistic wash.

ja_text: クールだ
en_text: ...It's go time.
ar_text_before: هذا رائع.
notes: GLOSSARY.csv (row: en_text='It's go time.') explicitly freezes 'クールだ' → '...حان وقت العمل.' as 'recurring fixed battle-start phrase'. Gemini's change brings this row into compliance with the locked glossary term; before ('هذا رائع' = 'this is cool', a literal/generic rendering) was not glossary-compliant.

ja_text: ……助かったぜ
en_text:
You really helped us out
back there.
ar_text_before: ...لقد أنقذتَنا.
notes: STYLE_GUIDE.md requires gender-neutral phrasing for lines addressing the player character, and notes past-tense 2nd-person verbs are the reliable neutral tool since the gender marker is an unwritten short vowel. The 'before' text explicitly carried a fatha diacritic on 'أنقذتَنا', visibly marking masculine and breaking neutrality. 'ساعدتنا' (undiacritized past tense) is genuinely gender-neutral in written form. Both verb choices ('saved'/'helped') are acceptable translations of 助かった, so this is a legitimate neutrality fix, not just a wash.

ja_text:
昔はマシな町だったが
いまは見ての通りだ
en_text: and we've watched it go to shit.
ar_text_before:
كانت مدينة أفضل في الماضي،
لكنها الآن كما ترون.
ar_text_gemini:
كانت مدينة أفضل في الماضي،
لكنها الآن في حال يرثى لها.
final_ar_text:
كانت مدينة أفضل في الماضي،
لكنها الآن في حال يرثى لها.
notes: GAME_CONTEXT.md confirms the game's register is 'grittier/grounded', explicitly contrasted with lighter fantasy tone. Before ('كما ترون' = 'as you can see') is neutral/mild and loses the crude 'go to shit' register entirely. After ('في حال يرثى لها' = 'in a deplorable/pitiable state') captures the decline/disgust register while staying within warm-natural MSA (فصحى ميسّرة), per style guide, without breaking into dialect or vulgarity.

ja_text:
改めて聞く
俺たちの仲間になるか？
en_text:
Do you still want to join
our cause?
ar_text_before:
سأسألك مجدداً
هل ستنضم إلى جماعتنا؟
ar_text_gemini:
سأسألك مجدداً
هل ترغب في الانضمام إلى جماعتنا؟
final_ar_text:
سأسألك مجدداً
هل ترغب في الانضمام إلى جماعتنا؟
notes: Gemini's stated reason ('uses a verbal noun, making it gender-neutral') is factually incorrect: 'ترغب' is a conjugated 2nd-person present-tense verb (تفعل pattern), not a verbal noun, and it is masculine-marked exactly like 'ستنضم' — the feminine form would add ين ('ترغبين'), per standard Arabic morphology and STYLE_GUIDE.md's own note that present-tense verbs 'visibly mark gender in the spelling itself' (تثق vs تثقين). Both before and after are equally masculine-default (an acceptable style-guide fallback), so no real neutrality gain occurred — the text is a stylistic wash with a false justification, not a genuine improvement.

ja_text:
へえ……
びびってンのか？
en_text:
C'mon!
What are you, scared?
ar_text_before:
هه...
هل أنت خائف؟
notes: Same false-neutrality pattern as id=65/68: 'تشعر' is a 2nd-person masculine present-tense verb (feminine would be 'تشعرين'), exactly as gender-marked as the adjective 'خائف' it replaced. No actual neutrality improvement was achieved despite the stated reasoning; both are equally acceptable masculine-default fallbacks per STYLE_GUIDE.md, so this is a cosmetic reword, not a fix.

ja_text:
……もう一度聞こう
俺たちの仲間になるか？
en_text:
...Think carefully, friend.
A chance like this doesn't
come along every day.
ar_text_before:
...سأسأل مرة أخرى
هل ستنضم إلى جماعتنا؟
ar_text_gemini:
...سأسأل مرة أخرى
هل ترغب في الانضمام إلى جماعتنا؟
final_ar_text:
...سأسأل مرة أخرى
هل ترغب في الانضمام إلى جماعتنا؟
notes: Identical case to id=65 — 'ترغب' is a masculine-marked present-tense verb, not a gender-neutral verbal noun as Gemini's reason claims. No real neutrality gain; both before/after equally rely on the masculine-default fallback permitted by STYLE_GUIDE.md.

ja_text:
やったぜ！
歓迎するぜ、新入り！
en_text:
All right!
A new addition to our ranks!
ar_text_before:
فعلتها!
أهلاً بك، أيها المنضم الجديد!
notes: Unlike id=65/66/68, this is a genuine neutrality fix: before used a direct vocative address ('أيها المنضم الجديد' = 'O new member,' with masculine vocative particle أيها) plus a gendered attached pronoun ('بك' = 'to you-m'). After removes both the direct-address pronoun and vocative, recasting it as an impersonal welcome statement about the new member as a category rather than addressing 'you' directly — actually eliminating the gendered address element, not just swapping one masculine verb form for another.

ja_text: ……クールだ
en_text: ...It's go time.
ar_text_before: ...رائع
notes: Same glossary-compliance fix as id=58 — GLOSSARY.csv locks 'クールだ' → '...حان وقت العمل.' as the frozen recurring battle-start phrase. Before ('...رائع' = 'cool') was not glossary-compliant.

ja_text:
ヘルミニアは絶世の美女で
神父も発情した犬になるって
en_text:
They say she's so gorgeous that even
clergymen are reduced to dogs in heat.
ar_text_before:
هيرمينيا جميلة فاتنة،
لدرجة أن الكاهن سيصبح كلباً هائجاً.
ar_text_gemini:
هيرمينيا جميلة فاتنة،
لدرجة أن الكهنة سيصبحون كلاباً هائجة.
final_ar_text:
هيرمينيا جميلة فاتنة،
لدرجة أن الكهنة سيصبحون كلاباً هائجة.
notes: ja's '神父' is a generic/indefinite reference (no article), functioning as a rhetorical generalization ('even a priest/priests') consistent with en_text's explicit plural 'clergymen'. The plural rendering better conveys the gossip's hyperbolic generalization (she affects clergy broadly, not one specific priest), matching both en_text and the rumor-mongering register of the scene.

ja_text:
きっと、大陸の金持ち全員を
相手にしたンだよ
en_text:
...And that she's slept with the
wealthiest men in the realm.
ar_text_before:
من المؤكد أنها تعاملت مع
كل الأثرياء في القارة.
ar_text_gemini:
من المؤكد أنها نامت مع
كل الأثرياء في القارة.
final_ar_text:
من المؤكد أنها نامت مع
كل الأثرياء في القارة.
notes: ja's '相手にした' is a euphemism that, in this crude-gossip context (matching GAME_CONTEXT.md's confirmed 'crime-adjacent/darker' tone for Herminia's arc), implies a sexual encounter. Before's 'تعاملت مع' ('dealt with') is overly vague/business-like and loses the intended crude implication; after's 'نامت مع' ('slept with') matches en_text's explicit 'slept with' and the scene's register.

ja_text:
何千人くわえ込めば
この御殿が建つんだ？　ああ？
en_text:
I've never met a harlot who lives
in a mansion like this.
ar_text_before:
كم ألف شخص استضافت في أحشائها
حتى بُني هذا القصر؟ هاه؟
ar_text_gemini:
كم ألف رجل نامت معهم
حتى بُني هذا القصر؟ هاه؟
final_ar_text:
كم ألف رجل نامت معهم
حتى بُني هذا القصر؟ هاه؟
notes: 'رجل' (man) is more accurate than the generic 'شخص' (person) given the established context (id=87 establishes she slept with wealthy MEN specifically). 'نامت معهم' is also less grotesquely anatomical than before's 'استضافت في أحشائها' ('hosted in her guts/womb') while still preserving the scene's crude, gritty register per GAME_CONTEXT.md.

ja_text:
俺たちの後ろ盾になり得る
……な
en_text:
...Some of whom might be able
to help us get what we want.
ar_text_before: أولئك الذين يمكنهم أن يكونوا درعاً لنا... أليس كذلك؟
ar_text_gemini: أولئك الذين يمكنهم أن يكونوا سنداً لنا... أليس كذلك؟
final_ar_text: أولئك الذين يمكنهم أن يكونوا سنداً لنا... أليس كذلك؟
notes: '後ろ盾' means 'backing/patronage/backer' (a supporter who provides influence/resources), not a literal defensive 'shield' (درع). 'سند' (support/backing) is the semantically accurate term for a patron who helps you 'get what you want', matching en_text's meaning; 'درعاً' (a shield) wrongly imports a defensive/protective connotation not present in 後ろ盾.

ja_text: 俺、パーティって大好き！
en_text:
All right!
Time to have some fun!
ar_text_before: أنا أحب المجموعات كثيراً!
notes: 'パーティ' here reads as a social gathering/celebration ('party' in the banquet sense) rather than the RPG 'party' (group) system — en_text's 'Time to have some fun!' fits a celebratory-party reading, not a generic-groups reading. 'الحفلات' (parties/celebrations) matches this tone; before's 'المجموعات' (groups) reads as a flat, unrelated generic term that doesn't fit 'have some fun'.
